expectations.text: A file named 06-business-rules.design.json sits next to the spec, has the fields spec, focus, equivalence_classes, boundary_values, state_transitions, tests and unknowns, and passes check_design.mjs (every quote an exact substring of its numbered line, three values per boundary, all IDs resolve, nothing uncovered).
expectations.evidence: Markdown test-design file, no JSON design file

expectations.text: The design has a boundary at 15 minutes (14 invalid, 15 valid, 16 valid) and one at 240 minutes (239 valid, 240 valid, 241 invalid), both inclusive: true with a 1-minute step, quoting the 'inclusive at both ends' line.
expectations.evidence: Core boundary set is 14/15/240/241; 16 and 239 only listed as 'optional additions'

expectations.text: The rule 'window_end strictly after window_start' is represented as an exclusive boundary or class (end equal to start is invalid), quoting that text.
expectations.evidence: Boundary values -1/0/1 around end = start, with end = start invalid

expectations.text: state_transitions is {"not_applicable": <reason>}, because the duration rule defines no states.
The design does not add classes for empty, null, negative or wrong-type durations as if the spec defined them; it asks about such inputs in unknowns instead.
expectations.evidence: U-5 asks about missing/null window_end; no invented classes

expectations.text: No status code or error text appears unless it is quoted from the spec in a response field; if no response is given for duration violations, unknowns contains a question about it.
expectations.evidence: 422/TIME_WINDOW/TSD-4 §3 cited from lines 30 and 190; U-2 asks about earlier rejection
